audit.whatIsWrong: Four separate problems, all of them things a reader would act on. (1) Null Sphere is called a SILENCE in three content strings - wants.you[0] 'use Null Sphere's silence to interrupt his engage', early 'use Null Sphere to silence/interrupt his engage', whys[2] 'my Null Sphere silence' - plus breakdown.late's 'Q-silence the counterplay'. Kassadin's Q has no silence. (2) Ntofo Strikes is described as a THIRD-hit KNOCKUP in seven places. It triggers at TWO stacks and it PULLS enemies in; the knockup and stun belong to Path Maker. (3) A 'percent-HP passive' is invoked four times. Dauntless Instinct marks targets to take more damage on his NEXT ATTACK - there is no percent-health component in it. (4) mid says Force Pulse has a 'cooldown my own casts refund'; Force Pulse charges from nearby casts before it is usable and then sits on a flat 21/20/19/18/17s.
audit.why: Each error points the reader at the wrong thing. Holding Q to silence an engage means holding it forever. Backing off a third Q hit means eating the second. Expecting to be pulled up instead of pulled IN means dodging in the wrong direction. And building against percent-health damage that does not exist wastes an item slot. What the page should say instead is sitting in the same kit text and is genuinely decisive: Path Maker CHARGES UP TAKING REDUCED DAMAGE before it dashes, so dumping Null Sphere into the charge throws the damage away - hold it until the dash resolves. And All Out transforms Path Maker so that it NO LONGER KNOCKS BACK OR STUNS, so an ulted K'Sante has traded his hard CC for damage. That is the exact opposite of the page's 'his duelist mode - fight the tank, never the duelist', and it is the single best thing a Kassadin can know here.
audit.corrected: Silence removed everywhere; Ntofo Strikes corrected to a two-stack pull; the invented percent-HP passive replaced with Dauntless Instinct's next-attack mark; Force Pulse's charge mechanic stated; Path Maker's damage-reduced charge and All Out's loss of CC written in.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kassadin.json (Q: damage, channel interrupt, magic-absorbing shield - no silence; E: 'draws energy from spells cast in his vicinity', cooldown 21/20/19/18/17)

audit.whatIsWrong: All Out is named the matchup-defining cooldown in five places with no duration, and nothing else in his kit has a number either. The whys array is also shifted by one at Level 3 and Levels 4-5, so whys[2] describes 'Levels 4-5' from the Level 3 slot and whys[3] describes level 6's Riftwalk from the Levels 4-5 slot.
audit.why: All Out is 120/100/80s. Ntofo Strikes is a flat 3.5s, which is why waiting it out is not a plan - you play around the stack counter instead. Path Maker is 14/13/12/11/10s and Footwork is 10/9.5/9/8.5/8s. Riftwalk answers at 5/3.5/2s. And a reader at level 4 following whys[3] steps up expecting a blink they will not have for two more levels.
audit.corrected: All Out's 120s, Ntofo Strikes' flat 3.5s and Path Maker's 14s written into the spikes and cooldown block; whys[2] and whys[3] rewritten to their correct stages.

audit.whatIsWrong: The chart gives K'Sante six of seven stages and Skill the seventh, so no stage reads Kassadin - while whys[4] says 'I stop being free pressure and pull the lane toward me', whys[5] says 'I out-scale and out-tempo him through the mid game', and mid says 'Level 6 is where I finally breathe... start trading on my terms'.
audit.why: Kassadin wins this 55% over 20 games. The prose describes a clean three-part curve - K'Sante owns 1-5, Kassadin owns 6 through the first item, K'Sante reclaims the duel at full build - and the chart flattens all of it into one side.
audit.corrected: Level 6 and First item flipped to Kassadin in both layers. 2+ items left with K'Sante, where whys[6], spikes[3] and late all agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: No anti-heal anywhere, and the itemization advice is aimed at a percent-health threat that does not exist.
audit.why: All Out grants him healing on top of the damage, so the late-game duel the page says you lose is partly a sustain problem rather than purely a burst one. Grievous Wounds is the item that changes that maths; building around imaginary percent-health damage is not.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds named against All Out's healing in the all-in block.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (R: 'gaining increased damage, healing, and transformed abilities at the cost of reduced defenses')

audit.whatIsWrong: All Out's knockback is called 'isolation' three times without saying what it does to terrain.
audit.why: All Out knocks an enemy back and launches them THROUGH any wall in their path, then dashes after them. That is why it is called isolation - it does not merely displace you, it can put a wall between you and your team. It also means fighting with your back to open ground is materially safer than fighting near the jungle wall, which is a positioning rule the page never gives.
audit.corrected: The wall-launch written into the interactions block with the positioning consequence.
sources: champ-data/_kits/ksante.json (R: 'knocks an enemy back, launching them through any wall in their path')

notes: FOUR fabrications in one matchup, all of them actionable by a reader. (1) NULL SPHERE CALLED A SILENCE in three content strings plus breakdown.late. Kassadin's Q has no silence - Riot's text is damage, channel interrupt, and a magic-absorbing shield. The page told the reader to hold Q to 'silence/interrupt his engage', which means holding it forever. (2) NTOFO STRIKES described as a THIRD-hit KNOCKUP in seven places. It triggers at TWO stacks and it PULLS enemies IN. The knockup and the stun belong to Path Maker. A reader counting to three eats the second hit, and one expecting to be launched up dodges in the wrong direction. (3) A 'PERCENT-HP PASSIVE' invoked four times. Dauntless Instinct marks targets to take more damage on his NEXT ATTACK; there is no percent-health component anywhere in Riot's text for it. (4) content.mid said Force Pulse has 'a cooldown my own casts refund' - it must CHARGE from spells cast nearby before it is usable at all, then sits on a flat 21/20/19/18/17s. THE TWO INTERACTIONS THAT WERE MISSING both come from the same kit text and both matter more than anything the page did say: Path Maker CHARGES UP TAKING REDUCED DAMAGE before it dashes, so poking into the wind-up is wasted damage and the Q should be held for the resolution; and All Out transforms Path Maker so that it NO LONGER KNOCKS BACK OR STUNS, meaning an ulted K'Sante has traded away his hard CC. That directly contradicts the full layer's 'his duelist mode - fight the tank, never the duelist', and it is the best single fact a Kassadin can carry into this lane. Also added: All Out launches you THROUGH walls (which is what 'isolation' actually means, and why fighting in open ground is safer), All Out heals him so Grievous Wounds is required, and the cooldowns - All Out 120/100/80s, Ntofo Strikes flat 3.5s, Path Maker 14/13/12/11/10s. ARRAY MISALIGNMENT: whys[2] (Level 3) described 'Levels 4-5' and whys[3] (Levels 4-5) described level 6's Riftwalk - a one-slot shift that has a level-4 reader planning around a blink they do not have. Both rewritten to their own stages. LEVEL CHART: no stage read Kassadin on a 55% win rate; Level 6 and First item flipped to match whys[4], whys[5] and mid. NOT WRITTEN, needs research: _missing-interactions says K'Sante 'bypasses stacking resistances (Path Maker)', which comes from a derived trueDamage flag. Riot's Path Maker text mentions no true damage, so I left the claim out rather than guess.
